definitions.explanation: A layer of fabric placed between the outer fabric and lining of a garment to add stiffness, shape, and structure. Used in collars, cuffs, waistbands, and other parts that need to hold their form.

examples.japanese: {襟|えり}に{芯地|しんじ}を{入|い}れる。
この{芯地|しんじ}はアイロンで{接着|せっちゃく}するタイプだ。
examples.english: This interfacing is the iron-on type.

examples.japanese: スーツの{仕立|した}てには{適切|てきせつ}な{芯地|しんじ}を{選|えら}ぶことが{仕上|しあ}がりを{左右|さゆう}する。
examples.english: Choosing the right interlining in suit tailoring determines the quality of the finished product.

notes:
A tailoring and sewing term composed of {芯|しん} (core) and {地|じ} (cloth, fabric). Interlining is essential in garment construction, especially for structured clothing like suits, jackets, and dress shirts. There are two main types: {接着芯|せっちゃくしん} (fusible/iron-on interfacing) and {縫|ぬ}い{付|つ}け{芯|しん} (sew-in interfacing).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {接着|せっちゃく}{芯地|しんじ}: fusible interlining (iron-on type)
- {芯地|しんじ}を{貼|は}る: to apply interlining
- {芯地|しんじ}を{入|い}れる: to insert interlining
- {不織布|ふしょくふ}{芯地|しんじ}: non-woven interlining

RELATED TERMS:
- {接着芯|せっちゃくしん}: fusible interfacing — commonly shortened from {接着|せっちゃく}{芯地|しんじ}
- {裏地|うらじ}: lining — the fabric on the inside of a garment, distinct from interlining
